question:
Consider the homogeneous system
$$x+y+z=0$$
$$x+ky+z=0$$
$$x+y+kz=0$$

(a) Evaluate the determinant of the coefficient matrix in terms of $k$.

(b) Determine the values of $k$ for which the system has only the trivial solution.

(c) For the remaining value of $k$, determine the number of solutions and express them using two parameters.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient determinant is
$$D= egin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\1 & k & 1\1 & 1 & k\end{vmatrix}$$
Apply $R_2 o R_2-R_1$ and $R_3 o R_3-R_1$:
$$D= egin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\0 & k-1 & 0\0 & 0 & k-1\end{vmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$D=(k-1)^2$$

(b)
A homogeneous system has only the trivial solution when its coefficient determinant is non-zero.
$$D eq0\Rightarrow(k-1)^2 eq0$$
Therefore, the system has only the trivial solution
$$x=y=z=0$$
when $k eq1$.

(c)
When $k=1$, all three equations become
$$x+y+z=0$$
Thus, only one independent equation remains and the system has infinitely many solutions.
Let $y=s$ and $z=t$. Then
$$x=-s-t$$
Hence, the solutions are
$$x=-s-t,\quad y=s,\quad z=t,\quad s,t\in\mathbb{R}$$

options.A:
(a) $D=(k+1)^2$
(b) Only the trivial solution for $k\neq-1$
(c) For $k=-1$, $x=-s-t,\ y=s,\ z=t$
options.B:
(a) $D=(k-1)^2$
(b) Only the trivial solution for $k\neq1$
(c) For $k=1$, infinitely many solutions $x=-s-t,\ y=s,\ z=t,\ s,t\in\mathbb{R}$
options.C:
(a) $D=k(k-1)$
(b) Only the trivial solution for $k\neq0,1$
(c) For $k=0$ or $1$, infinitely many solutions
options.D:
(a) $D=(k-1)^2$
(b) Only the trivial solution when $k=1$
(c) For $k\neq1$, infinitely many solutions
